_readme: THE LANE MAP (ADR 095). One register naming each CI lane and the paths that make it run.
tooling/ci/lane-detect.mjs --lane <name> is the `detect` job of each lane's callee workflow
(.github/workflows/lane-<name>.yml): it answers affected=true on a push to main, on any event that
is not a pull_request, on a changed path this map does not name at all, and whenever the diff
cannot be read; otherwise affected is true only when a changed path matches that lane's globs.
tooling/ci/lane-verdict.mjs is each callee's always-run tail job, and the only licence it gives a
skipped work job is detect's affected=false.
`unclaimed` names paths no lane grades beyond the guards that always run: a change touching only
these runs no lane. A path matching NEITHER a lane nor `unclaimed` is unmapped, and an unmapped
path runs every lane: the map failing open is the safe direction.
A lane's globs name everything its jobs READ, not only the directory they build: the Worker
tests read every workflow file, the ops register and one Dart source, so those are workers paths.
`lane-detect.mjs --check` (guard-meta) fails on a tracked file no entry claims and on a glob that
matches no tracked file. Glob syntax: `**` spans directories, `*` stays inside one path segment.
A lane's `callee`, when present, is the workflow whose detect job runs `lane-detect.mjs --lane
<name>`, and --check fails when that file is missing or names another lane.
Only `workers` has a callee today (extensions-ci.yml keeps its own discover job until it adopts
lane-detect); the other lanes' globs are written now so that `unmapped` means new to the map,
not a lane that has not moved yet (O-CI-LANES-NOT-CALLABLE-UNITS).
